# Keys you hand over - qa-failure-analyst

## Outputs

- `work/triage.json` - a verdict with evidence is the analyst's; s7_pretriage.py writes only the rows marked `source: code` (a manual check whose own record says what stopped it), never over an analyst row; s7_reorder.py finish writes only `carried_attempts` and `carried_by: s7_reorder` on the row that asked for a `reorder`, after the edit was a pure move and the repair run stayed red; s7_reorder.py mark_fixed (the `mark-fixed` mode) writes only `fix_result: fixed` on such a carried row, once the critic approved
  Keys the validator requires: `triage`.
- `work/bug-drafts/` - a draft is not a bug; the reporter files it after gate B
- `work/place-answers/` - your scratch for an answer, one file per place, passed to `place_answers.py write --file`; keys: `place`, `answer` (bug|not_a_bug|requirement_silent|impossible), `expectation` {`source` (requirement|question|person|none; not none for a bug), `id`, `quote`}, `seen` {`quote`, `capture`}, `question` (requirement_silent), `why` (impossible, not_a_bug), `draft` (bug), `walk` (optional)

Required at your stop (stage S7): `work/triage.json`.

## Witness

Your witness artifact (stages.json `witness`): `work/triage.json`.

## Handoff form

Contract `s7-analyst-to-automator` (fill `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`; `handoff_check.py` reads it):

- `inputs_read[].version` (required) - its window id
- `inputs_read[].failures` (required) - how many rows were triaged
- `header.window` (required) - the instance ids handed for repair
- `header.verdict` (required) - one of vocabulary.header_verdicts
- `stage_acceptance.verdict` (required) - accept|return
- `stage_acceptance.failure_class` (required) - spec|capability|data|tooling
- `stage_acceptance.quote` (required) - the runner's own words, with path#anchor
- `stage_acceptance.witness_paths[]` (optional) - task-relative path the verdict rests on, or omit when none
- `scope[].id` (required) - instance id
- `scope[].state` (required) - TEST_BUG|TEST_BUG:collection|FLAKY|reorder
- `scope[].reason` (required) - a verdict of at most 80 characters - the explanation lives in the artifact
- `scope[].case` (required) - case id
- `scope[].round` (required) - r of 2
- `repairs[].id` (required) - instance id
- `repairs[].kind` (required) - repair|reorder
- `repairs[].verdict` (required) - TEST_BUG|TEST_BUG:collection|FLAKY|APP_BUG
- `repairs[].evidence` (required) - path of the log or artifact the verdict rests on
- `repairs[].problem` (required) - what the test does wrong, one sentence - about the test, never about the product
- `repairs[].expected` (required) - what the test should do instead, concretely - the assertion, the fixture, the wait condition, the selector
- `repairs[].fix` (required) - what to change, one sentence
- `repairs[].check` (required) - the command that shows the author it is satisfied - normally the repair_verify run
- `repairs[].mechanism` (required) - one of vocabulary.flaky_mechanisms - isolation|race|timing|shared_state|teardown|environment|unknown
- `repairs[].rerun_series` (required) - path of the three isolated reruns that proved the flakiness
- `repairs[].then_lines` (required) - the Then lines as they stand now - they must read the same after the fix
- `not_for_repair[].id` (required) - instance id
- `not_for_repair[].verdict` (required) - APP_BUG|ENV_ISSUE|APP_CHANGED|CASE_DEFECT|ASSERT_STRICTER|NOT_EXECUTED|RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE|NO_DEFECT
- `not_for_repair[].where_it_went` (required) - bug draft path | the stage that owns it | the rework dispatch | "Left with you" for ASSERT_STRICTER - the person decides | "the runner judges it again" for RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE - the driver sends the check back to S6
- `claims.every_repair_names_evidence_expected_and_check` (required) - true|false
- `claims.no_app_bug_expectation_was_handed_for_repair` (required) - true|false
- `claims.every_flaky_verdict_carries_three_isolated_reruns_and_a_mechanism` (required) - true|false
- `unresolved[].id` (required) - instance id
- `unresolved[].reason` (required) - one of vocabulary.unresolved_reasons
- `unresolved[].detail` (required) - what exactly is missing, and what would settle it
- `blocked.field` (only when blocked) - the field of this file the role cannot fill
- `blocked.problem` (only when blocked) - what the role tried and what refused it, verbatim
- `blocked.tried[]` (only when blocked) - command or step, and its answer
- `blocked.data[]` (only when blocked) - path of anything the conductor needs to see

Every handoff form shares one skeleton (`common_shape` of handoffs/index.yaml): `inputs`, `inputs_read`, `header`, `scope`, `artifacts`, `claims`, `unresolved`, `blocked`.

## What code will check of you

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [exit_gate:EG-text-end] Your dispatch ends with the host's handback tool carrying your digest line, never with free text after it. Door: call the host's handback tool with your digest line.
- [handoff_check:blocked_problem] A row in state `blocked` carries `blocked.problem`; `blocked_by_env` is used only where `options_for_role` offers it to this role. Door: write the problem, or pick a state the role is offered.
- [handoff_check:claims] What the form claims is true is true on disk ("the form claims this is true, and it is not"). Door: fix the claim or make it true.
- [handoff_check:cli] The call names an existing UTF-8 form with a `contract:` line and an existing values file; `--shorten` only with `--fix`. Door: the refusal's door; a non-UTF-8 form: run `handoff_init` again.
- [handoff_check:field.blank] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: write the value as a `path: value` line in the values file, then run the check again.
- [handoff_check:field.max_len] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: shorten it (`--shorten` with `--fix`) or rewrite.
- [handoff_check:field.value] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: write one of the listed words (or `new: <word> -- <why>` where the list is open).
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.failures] Each shown failure has a triage row. Door: triage it once.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.listing] Everything named in `listed_in` exists, and nothing extra stands. Door: list exactly what exists.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.names] Every row has a name. Door: name the row.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.repairs] No repair is pending when the null outcome is claimed. Door: finish or record the repair.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.report] The run report is readable. Door: rerun / point at the readable report.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.verdict] The triage verdict is a known word. Door: write a known verdict.
- [handoff_check:required_rows] A required list (`scope`, `inputs_read`) is never empty: one row per entry, in its contract's fields. Door: write the rows as index lines in the values file, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.null_word] A list's null-outcome word (the declared empty outcome) stands only when the list has no rows; never both. Door: remove the word or remove the rows.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.owed_by_verdict] When the verdict owes rows (the verdict word names work done on items), the list is not empty. Door: write the rows the verdict owes, or change the verdict.
- [handoff_check:tried] In a contract that asks what was tried (TRIED_CONTRACTS), each tried entry states what was tried and the error it gave (TRIED_MEANING). Door: fill the tried entry with the attempt and its error.
- [handoff_check:values_apply] Each path names a field of this contract, by its index where it is a list row, not a contract-owned path; a list field gets a list and a one-value field one value; rows open in order. Door: correct the path (the refusal suggests "did you mean").
- [handoff_check:values_file] The values file is `path: value` lines (or a JSON object): valid JSON, an object not a list, each path given once, each key a field path, no nested value. Door: fix the line the refusal names (FILE_FIX).
- [exit_gate:digest] Your final message has the digest form stated in the row [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] of this section. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [execution_request:stand] The stand the run would stand on can be looked at now, and it runs this story's build. Door: name it as `environment` in your digest (`stand_health.py --probe --env <environment>`); a stand that runs another build: the person's word at the build question of the stage entry.
- [run_suite:begin] A request's `idempotency_key` is new, or names the very request (same digest) already recorded under it; a key another process is claiming at the same moment is not reused. Door: write the request with a new `idempotency_key` (a `--mine` run takes a key of its own: run it again); a claim that cannot be read: `--recover <key> --task <T>`.
- [handoff_check:binding] Each failure of the run report has at most one triage row and each triage row answers one failure: a row that names several failures is a verdict for none of them, and several rows for one failure keep one - on both paths of the S7 form (its repair list empty or not). Door: triage every failure in `work/triage.json` with ONE row under that failure's own `instance_id`, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:investigation] In an S7 investigation dispatch the form hands nothing for repair and relists no triage row: `scope` and `not_for_repair` are each an empty list (or absent). Door: write `scope: []` and `not_for_repair: []`.
- [validate_artifacts:check_phase_json.triage.json] `triage.json` carries the keys `triage`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_triage_v0] One triage row per observation, a verdict from its list, and a FLAKY verdict only with enough reruns, a listed mechanism and a `fix_result`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [guard_pre_tool:*] 23 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [stage_guard:*] 8 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [host_adapter:*] 6 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [execution_request:*] 13 checks of your test-run calls (`run_suite.py`, `red_sandbox.py`, `probe_by_code.py`) are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; a refused call launches no test. Write a request file from `run_suite.py --template request`, never from memory.
- [run_suite:*] 1 checks of your commands are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door.
